s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with significant decreases in blood pressure post-exercise
salient_findings: Rapid dyspnea within 45 seconds of exercise initiation
Decreases in systolic and diastolic blood pressure post-exercise
Well-defined mass within the lower SVC with extension to the interatrial septum
key_facts: 66-year-old female with history of epilepsy, thyroid cancer, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea
Progressively worsening dyspnea on exertion over 9 months
No associated lower extremity edema, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, or lightheadedness
Lifetime nonsmoker
Normal left ventricular ejection fraction of 60% to 65%
Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum present
Normal pulmonary function tests
SVC peak flow velocity: 74 cm/s cephalad to mass, 124 cm/s caudal to mass
Narrowing of the SVC and decreased blood flow through the site of compression
